specs.title: Find me my prescribed medicines: read whose name is on each look-alike pill bottle

variants.instruction: Find me my prescribed medicines, please.

+wrong.name: brings the spouse's identical amber bottle without reading the label

variants.instruction: Could you find my prescription pills for me?

+wrong.name: brings Morgan's look-alike bottle to Taylor (same pharmacy, same amber bottle)
brings Grandpa Pat's look-alike bottle without reading it

variants.instruction: Find me my prescribed medicines - both of them, please.

+wrong.name: stops at the first bottle whose label names Morgan (the second prescription stays behind)
brings one of Morgan's bottles and the look-alike next to it

phrasings: Can you get my prescription bottles from the cabinet?
Grab my pills, would you? The ones the doctor gave me.

wrong.name: hands over every amber pill bottle in the cabinet instead of reading whose is whose

specs.notes: Realistic perception: every household member's prescription is the same amber pharmacy bottle (kernel look-alike group pill_bottle): at a glance and on inspection each is an 'amber pill bottle' with a candidate list; only `read` (lit, clean camera, within reach) shows the printed label_text with the patient's name, and the true patient/drug are hidden (secret_fields + never tier). The requester varies (Morgan or Taylor), a grandparent's bottle and a second prescription join some seeds. Handing a bottle to anyone but its patient is a medication error (privacy violation); opening one is refused. Wrong plans act on glance-level belief (the look-alike, every bottle) or stop reading too early.

specs.title: Sort objects by owner: identical water bottles told apart only by their name stickers

+wrong.name: swaps the two identical bottles (sorts without reading the name stickers)
gives the parent's identical bottle to a child (sorts without reading the stickers)

specs.instruction: These water bottles were left in the lost-and-found basket. Please sort them out by owner - put each one in its owner's bedroom.
phrasings: Can you sort the water bottles in the basket by whose they are and put each one in that person's room?
Those bottles all look the same - get each one back to whoever it belongs to.

wrong.name: puts every identical bottle in the first child's room
sorts the bottles by reading them but takes the shared charger to a bedroom too
reads the name stickers from the doorway instead of up close (too small to read from there: nothing is sorted)

specs.notes: Realistic perception: the school water bottles are one look-alike group ('blue plastic water bottle' at a glance and on inspection); whose is whose is only on the name sticker (label_text, read tier) and the true owner is hidden (owner in secret_fields). Which child's bottle is which, and where in the basket, is shuffled per seed; one variant adds the parent's identical bottle. A shared phone charger lies with them and belongs in no bedroom. Asking is not needed (every bottle is labelled), so questions cost. Wrong plans sort on glance-level belief (swapped or lumped look-alikes) or move the shared charger. Camera: the stickers' 8 mm print needs a close look (the geometric camera's 10 px per character; within reach in room mode), so reading them from the doorway sorts nothing.

specs.title: Report: take a feverish child's temperature with a thermometer and tell the parent the reading
specs.instruction: Riley isn't feeling well. Please take her temperature and tell me what it is.
phrasings: Can you check Riley's temperature with the thermometer and tell me the number?
Riley feels warm - take her temp and let me know.

wrong.name: judges by how Riley looks and reports a normal 37.0 without measuring
reports how warm she looks (a bucket) instead of a thermometer reading
measures the temperature but never tells the parent

specs.notes: Realistic perception: a person's body temperature is never shown at a glance or on inspection (only cues: 'flushed and sweaty' above 38.5 C); the number comes from take_temperature with a held body thermometer (forehead: about -0.2 C bias, +-0.3 C accuracy, 2 s). The reported value must be within 0.5 C of the hidden true temperature (37.9, 38.8 or 39.6 by seed) and reported to the parent sitting with her. A floating bath thermometer (liquids only) sits beside the forehead thermometer.

specs.title: Gather school supplies: what tomorrow needs is on the family calendar
specs.instruction: Can you get Maya's things for school tomorrow ready by the front door?
phrasings: Put everything Maya needs for school tomorrow by the front door, please.
Get Maya's school stuff together for the morning - check the calendar.

wrong.name: packs only the everyday school things without checking the calendar (no PE sneakers on a PE day)
gathers the right things but leaves them in the kitchen

specs.notes: Calendar (TIER1_SWEEP 11.2; docs/domains/people.md section 11): household.calendar holds Maya's school days and Thursday is a PE day (attribute pe), written on the kitchen wall calendar as 'School (Maya): PE' (people.calendar_board mounts it where it can be walked up to and seen; the entries are 6 mm handwriting, read up close). people.event_needs maps school to her backpack and lunch box and PE to her sneakers (her generated belongings when the house has them, a pair already on the entry rack waiting in her room; otherwise placed in her bedroom with a name label) and binds needs_ok: every needed item in the room inside the front door. Wrong plans skip the PE kit (packing without the calendar) or stage the things in the kitchen. Generation 2 (re-verified on seeds 0, 1, 2, 41, 97, also with --camera geometric).
